remarks: Saudel is back. It dropped below tropical-storm strength after the 28 Aug Zhejiang landfall and was carried last run as an unnamed depression; JMA has now re-named it and it is crossing the northern South China Sea eastward, passing south of Yantian tonight and the Taiwan Strait approaches in about two days.
No tracked port is suspended. Yantian and Xiamen are on watch only, and no carrier or terminal has announced a closure for this phase of the storm.

Two other systems are active but neither comes near a tracked port, so they are left out of the incoming table: an unnamed depression south of Japan forecast to reach tropical-storm strength around the Amami islands, and Bang-lang, now a weak low far east of Japan.

The Shanghai/Ningbo weather entry expires after 1 Sep by design. That is the right call for the weather story, but the congestion picture is going the wrong way — 1.68M TEU at anchorage on 30 Aug against a queue-to-berth ratio of 3.24, the worst reading in the tracked set by a wide margin and up 0.71 in a single day.

SEKO has not refreshed its monitoring page since 28 Aug and Kuehne+Nagel has not published a new weekly edition, so every berth waiting figure on this page is at least three days old and is labelled with its source date rather than re-estimated.
